conclusion.scope: The codec-validate GPU kernel called ScalarCodec<E4M3Fn>::decode for all 256 byte codes in a gfx1201-targeted binary on the recorded exact gfx1201 device.
conclusion.qualification: The E4M3 comparison is not an independent validation of native conversion semantics: both reference and candidate call the same gfx1201 native builtin.

native_decode_source.semantics: The E4M3Fn specialization dispatches decode() to __builtin_amdgcn_cvt_f32_fp8(int(bits), 0) when __gfx1201__ is defined. Its source fallback explicitly maps signed zero, E4M3 subnormals as mantissa * 2^-9, 0x7f/0xff to NaN, and other normal codes by FP32 exponent/mantissa assembly. The gfx1201 branch delegates those conversions to the native builtin.

coverage_limits: The probe compares ScalarCodec<E4M3Fn>::decode with phase85_m1_branchless::decode_e4m3; both select __builtin_amdgcn_cvt_f32_fp8(bits, 0) under __gfx1201__, so zero mismatches do not independently establish the builtin's values.
Finite outputs are compared bitwise and NaNs by class; payload/sign behavior for NaN is not established by this comparator.
This is an exhaustive scalar-code probe, not a model/MTP matmul result or proof that model inputs hit each code.

stage_c1_correction.premise: Forcing sllm_matmul_mxfp8_w8a8_m1_col2_body into its #else branch is not a pure native-versus-software decode test.
stage_c1_correction.reason: The #else branch calls BlockCodec::load -> decode_scaled. That helper uses integer exponent assembly for normal finite values whose scaled FP32 exponent is in range, but falls back to ScalarCodec<E4M3Fn>::decode for zero/subnormal/NaN and scaled underflow/overflow; that decode remains native on gfx1201. The #else also changes wave-shared scale loading to per-element scale handling.
stage_c1_correction.recommendation: Keep the gfx1201 col2 body and scale/layout path fixed. Add a diagnostic compile-time override for ScalarCodec<E4M3Fn>::decode that forces the existing software E4M3FN mapping for every code, then compare native and software builds on identical inputs. This isolates conversion from scale sharing and avoids native fallback on exceptional codes.

conclusions: Continuous logits metrics do not establish a uniform gfx1201 MXFP8 fidelity advantage: relative L2 is about 0.76% lower, but own-BF16-top1 absolute error is higher.
BF16 margins are not systematically larger on gfx1201, and low flip overlap alone does not identify a cause.

Independent 256-code scalar decode checks pass on both GPUs. On gfx1201, col2 software decode, activation software encode and KV software encode each preserve all 8 hidden/logits hashes and all 2048 top1 choices.
The generic-attention control changes some gfx1201 target hidden values but does not make them match gfx1030. The remaining target/companion arithmetic-path attribution is unresolved.
The investigation closes with scoped negative results, as permitted by the original acceptance criteria. No production kernel/default was adopted.
